To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of patients in the study did not have a good knowledge of the relationship between diet and cancer risk, that they were not aware of the importance of the Mediterranean diet and the benefits of physical activity, that they had a low intake of fruits and vegetables, and that the majority of the participants were overweight and had high blood pressure.

(i) the majority of patients with cancer do not receive the nutrition care that is recommended; (ii) nutrition care is provided in a variety of ways and settings; and (iii) the impact of nutrition intervention on outcomes is variable.

A diet low in fat, high in fiber, and rich in fruits and vegetables, along with a regular program of physical activity, is associated with a lower risk of developing colorectal cancer and may reduce the risk of other cancers.
